events.summary:
* WHAT...High surf expected. Water levels of 2 to 4 feet above
the normal high tide line, peaking during high tide.

* WHERE...Western Arctic Coast from Point Hope south.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Thursday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A low in the Western Bering Sea will send
a front moving east in the coast, resulting in south to
southeast winds ramping up Thursday morning through Friday,
before diminishing through Saturday. Sea levels will remain
elevated through Friday before gradually subsiding Friday
night into Saturday.

isolated thunderstorms along a line extending from Bisma Township to
near Morey. Movement was southeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Houghton Lake, Grayling, Ossineke, Roscommon, Lewiston, St. Helen,
The Town Of Hubbard Lake, Mio, Atlanta, Prudenville, Lachine, Comins,
Sharon, Frederic, McKinley, Long Rapids, Hillman, Lovells, Curran,
and North Higgins Lake.

events.region: Beartooth Ranger District Custer National Forest; Sheridan County/Casper BLM; Bighorn National Forest
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The National Weather Service in Billings has issued a Fire Weather
Watch...which is in effect from Friday afternoon through Friday
evening.

* IMPACTS: Low humidities, unseasonably warm temperatures, and
strong gusty winds will create erratic fire behavior for new or
existing fires.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In North Central WY Fire Zones...274...284.
In South Central MT Fire Zone...126.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In North Central WY...Big Horn...Johnson...Sheridan...Washakie.
In South Central MT...Carbon...Park...Stillwater...Sweet Grass.

* WIND: Southwest 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 10 percent.

* TEMPERATURES: Up to 88 degrees.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS: The worst conditions are expected across
the lower to middle elevations in fine fuels.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Cameron County in deep south Texas...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 528 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Port Of Brownsville, Southmost, Cameron Park, Downtown
Brownsville, Brownsville, Lincoln Park, Rivera High School, El
Jardin Elementary School, South Point, Brownsville South Padre
Island International Airport, Perkins Middle School, Villa
Pancho, Gonzalez Elementary School, North Brownsville Little
League, Lopez High School, Southmost Elementary School, Gallegos
Elementary School, Besteiro Middle School, Brownsville Public
Library Southmost Branch and Brownsville Fire Department Station
Six.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
